intent: A river drawn, not a country filled: the main stem draws itself across the continent on the reveal, three discharge bars make the Nile look like a creek, a split holds the fifth-of-all-water fact against the mouth width, and a boat rides the line to the sea for the 1500 Sweet Sea story.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which river carries the MOST water?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which river carries the most water?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: The Amazon. It pours 209,000 cubic metres into the Atlantic every second, a fifth of all river water on Earth.

lines.direction: ease back so the whole basin sits in frame; three discharge bars rise on 'Congo' with the Amazon off the chart; the Egyptian flag-ball thinks on 'Nile'; a tiny-stream sticker on 'barely' as the river line re-draws
lines.text: The Congo, next, moves about 41,000. The Nile, the longest river, barely 3,000.

lines.direction: hold wide; the length tag and a mountain sticker on 'Andes'; the Mouth pin and tag on 'mouth'; the 1 IN 5 / 320 KM split lands on 'wide'
lines.text: From the Andes it runs 6,400 kilometres to a mouth over 300 kilometres wide.

lines.direction: drift east toward the mouth; a boat rides the drawn line from mid-river to the sea until 'sweet'; a sailor sticker on 'captain'; the 1500 card on 'fresh'; the Brazilian flag-ball grins on 'sweet'; the Mouth pin leaves at the end
lines.text: In 1500 a Spanish captain found fresh water out of sight of land, and called it the Sweet Sea.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A fifth of all river water. Follow us.
